rows.summary: Robustness in physical records is achieved when system pointer states are redundantly encoded into environmental degrees of freedom, enabling independent observers to reach consensus. This process, formalizable through Spectrum Broadcast Structures (SBS) and quantum Darwinism, effectively 'broadcasts' information. Furthermore, thermodynamic constraints, specifically the energy cost of erasing information (Landauer's principle), bound the long-term stability of these records in both classical and quantum substrates.
